Recent research supports ranking diagnostics stratified by item popularity: a 2024 sequential-recommendation study comparing six negative samplers found aggregate accuracy concealed head/mid/tail disparities; uniform sampling favored head items, while popularity-based sampling offered more balanced performance with accuracy tradeoffs. [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276). Sampled evaluation can also reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation—even with popularity sampling—so sampled HR@10 should not be interpreted as catalog retrieval quality. [Dallmann et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045). Research on correcting sampled rank estimates further demonstrates that negative sampling introduces consequential ranking bias. [Subbiah et al., 2024](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/).

Recommended diagnostic design: construct auxiliary chronological prefix holdouts exclusively from training histories; report HR@10, reciprocal rank, and target-rank percentiles by training-item frequency and history length, including slice counts. Compare identical targets under fixed sampled candidates and full unseen catalogs; measure per-user rank correlation and model-order agreement separately. Estimate paired improvement intervals by resampling users within each category and recomputing the four-category macro-average; these intervals capture user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed variability. Controlled retraining ablations should change one component at a time: embedding normalization/regularization, sequence encoder versus last-item or pooled-history baselines, and negative sampler with matched training budgets. Treat inference-time perturbations as sensitivity checks rather than causal attribution; sequence shuffling can confound user-order patterns with item availability. [RecSys 2025 study](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/). These are proposed checks, not measured findings. Keep all auxiliary diagnostics separate from selection: retain the pinned macro validation HR@10 protocol unchanged.
